transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because I'm having some trouble at my job. I work as a cashier, and lately at the register, I keep getting stuck doing things that just... don't really fit the moment. 

Like, I'll start tapping the scanner in a certain pattern, or I'll just freeze completely with my hand hovering over the cash drawer while the customer is standing right there waiting for me. It's frustrating. It's been happening enough that, well, last week it actually got me written up by my manager. So I figured I needed to come in and figure out what's going on.
When you get stuck tapping or freezing, does it feel like you have to do it to relieve a bad feeling or prevent something from feeling wrong?

No, it's not really like that. I don't feel anxious or like something bad will happen if I don't do it. It's just... I just do it. Or I just freeze. There's no real feeling attached to it before it happens, I just kind of realize I'm doing it, or that I'm stuck.
Right before you tap or freeze, do you feel a build-up or urge in your body that gets relieved once it happens?

No, I don't feel anything like that. There's no build-up or... physical urge in my body at all. It doesn't feel like a pressure that I'm relieving. Like I said, I just kind of find myself doing it, or I just freeze up. There's really no warning or feeling right before it happens.
When one of these freezing or tapping episodes happens, are you fully aware of what’s going on around you?

Yeah, I'm fully aware. I know exactly where I am and what's happening. I can see the customer, I know they're waiting for their change or for me to scan their items. I can hear the sounds in the store. I'm just... stuck. My body just isn't doing what I want it to do, or it's doing this repetitive tapping thing instead. But my mind is right there the whole time.
Since you were a child, have you had trouble understanding social cues or knowing how to interact with other people?

No, I wouldn't say that. I've always been pretty normal when it comes to talking to people. I had friends growing up, and I do fine talking to customers at the store. I've never really had a problem understanding what people mean or how to act around them.
When you freeze or start tapping, does it ever feel like someone or something outside you is controlling your body?

No, it doesn't feel like that. I don't feel like anyone else is making me do it or... pulling the strings, I guess. It's just my body not cooperating with me. I know it's me, it's just... I can't stop it or start moving again when I want to. But it's definitely not some outside force controlling me.
Do you ever hear voices that other people can’t hear?

Yeah, actually. Most days, I hear what sounds like a couple of people talking... just off to the side of me. Sometimes they're calling my name, like from the stockroom, or they'll say I rang something up wrong. But when I turn around to look, there's nobody there. And... well, I'll ask my coworkers or a customer if they heard it, and they never do. So, yeah, I guess I do hear things other people don't.
Do you believe that other people are deliberately trying to send you messages through those voices?

No, I don't think so. It doesn't feel like a secret message or anything like that. Like I said, it just sounds like normal, everyday things... someone calling my name or mentioning the cash register. I don't think there's anyone deliberately trying to send me signals through them, no. They're just voices.
When you talk with other people, do they ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or doesn’t make sense?

No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever mentioned anything like that to me. I talk to customers all day at the register, and my coworkers, and... well, we seem to understand each other just fine. Sometimes I might lose my train of thought for a second, but they don't look at me like I'm not making sense. So, no, I don't think my speech is hard to follow.
Have you noticed yourself feeling much less interested in things or emotionally flat lately?

Yeah, I guess I have noticed that. I mean, I still care about my wife and kids, of course. But lately... I just don't have the push to do much. Like, I don't even feel like calling my son at college, which isn't like me. And I used to meet up with this kayak group, or tinker with little repair projects in the garage, but now I just... don't. I don't really have the energy or interest for it. My wife asks me what's wrong, and I mostly just shrug. I can't really find much to say about it, honestly. I just feel kind of empty.
